literal: Met hostile fate, yet affairs turned round; the old realm followed the ode Gathering Calamus.
idiomatic: Fate turned hostile, yet affairs wheeled about—and the old realm went the way of Gathering Calamus.

literal: First the ruler was deposed and the chancellor executed; at last the court changed and the market shifted.
idiomatic: First they deposed the ruler and killed the chancellor; in the end the court changed hands and the market changed with it.

literal: (Upon reaching Ye he happened on Chen's rise and Liang's fall, and so could not return south.)
idiomatic: (When he reached Ye, Chen was rising and Liang was falling, and he could not go home to the south.)

literal: Thus he lingered on the Zhang's banks, privately lamenting how it would ever end.
idiomatic: So he stayed stranded on the Zhang's shore, privately asking when the waiting would ever end.

literal: He declined the yellow swan's wheeling return; he felt shamed before the azure phoenix towering high.
idiomatic: He refused the yellow swan's wheeling homeward flight and felt small before the azure phoenix on its height.

literal: Never had he Wei Lingsi's gift for reply; in vain he stole Yan Xianzhi's post—compiling books beside the Hall where Culture Flourishes, awaiting edict in the quarter honored for letters.
idiomatic: He never had Wei Lingsi's wit in debate, only borrowed Yan Xianzhi's post in name—compiling books by the Flourishing Culture Hall, awaiting edict in the quarter where letters were honored.

literal: (In Wuping of Qi more than thirty gentlemen awaiting edict at the Forest of Literature were appointed, including Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi, Zu Xiaozheng, and others; Zhitui had sole charge, and works such as the Repair the Culture Hall Imperial Overview and the Continuation of Literary Genres Classification were all presented at the Gate of Advancing Worthies.)
idiomatic: (In Qi's Wuping era over thirty awaiting-edict gentlemen of the Forest of Literature were appointed, from Vice Director Yang Xiuzhi and Zu Xiaozheng downward; Zhitui held sole charge, and works such as the Repair the Culture Hall Imperial Overview and the Continuation of Literary Genres Classification were all submitted at the Gate of Advancing Worthies.)

literal: Wearing marten tail and cicada badge he took his place in rank; bearing canopy and halberd he entered the sequence.
idiomatic: He pinned marten tail and cicada badge and took his place in the ranks; he bore canopy and halberd and entered the court sequence.

literal: (At the time he was transferred from unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry to gentleman of the Yellow Gate.)
idiomatic: (At the time he was promoted from unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry to gentleman of the Yellow Gate.)

literal: He called on an old friend who had been chancellor alone—
idiomatic: He paid a visit to an old friend, the chancellor who stood alone—

literal: (The old friend, Vice Director Zu, managed secrets, issuing and receiving the emperor's commands.)
idiomatic: (That friend was Vice Director Zu, who held the secrets of state and shaped what the emperor sent out and took in.)

literal: and congratulated himself on a sovereign's intimate trust.
idiomatic: and counted himself blessed with a sovereign's intimate trust.

literal: Only night talk drew suspicion; could clutching a jade disk really suffice?
idiomatic: Even whispered talk after dark drew suspicion; could clutching a jade disk really keep one safe?

literal: He guarded against remonstrance and slander's spears and shields; he was wary of perilous hearts like mountain rivers.
idiomatic: He braced against remonstrance and slander, spear and shield alike, and watched hearts treacherous as mountain rivers.

literal: Through heavy furs cold was overcome; by removing fuel boiling ceased.
idiomatic: Heavy furs could beat back the cold; take away the fuel and the boil stops.

literal: (At the time the military despised literati; Zhitui enjoyed imperial favor and was wounded at every turn.)
idiomatic: (The military class then despised men of letters; Zhitui, though favored, was cut at every turn.)

literal: (Hence Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Jishu and six others were put to death for remonstrance; that day Zhitui barely escaped the neighboring disaster.)
idiomatic: (When Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Jishu and six others were executed for remonstrance, Zhitui that day barely escaped the disaster next door.)

literal: (Yet some of his peers slandered Zhitui to Vice Director Zu; the Vice Director investigated and found no substance, and treated him as before without forgetting.)
idiomatic: (Some peers still slandered Zhitui to Vice Director Zu; Zu investigated, found nothing, and kept his regard unchanged.)

literal: I traced Martial Completion's soaring wings, following the Spring Quarters back to origins.
idiomatic: I followed Martial Completion's soaring wings and traced the Spring Quarters back to their source.

literal: Only extravagance was cultivated; sycophant ministers were likewise deployed.
idiomatic: Only extravagance was tended; sycophant ministers were put to use as well.

literal: (Wucheng was extravagant; the inner palace had several hundred attendants, fed from land and water with rare tribute until they were sated and the surplus was cast into the privy.
idiomatic: (Wucheng was extravagant: several hundred women of the inner palace were fed from land and sea with rare tribute until they were glutted and the surplus was thrown into the privy.)

literal: Undergarments were all brocade and embroidery with pearls and jade, woven in sections of five hundred.
idiomatic: Even their undergarments were brocade and embroidery studded with pearl and jade, woven in lengths of five hundred.

literal: Afterward the inner palace took this as precedent.
idiomatic: After that the inner palace kept the custom.

literal: When the Later Sovereign was in the palace, he had Luotuopa's mother Lady Lu attend him, and Hu men such as He Hongzhen at his side; later they all took part in government and ruined the state.)
idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign was still in the palace, Luotuopa's mother Lady Lu and Hu favorites such as He Hongzhen stood at his side—and in time they all meddled in rule and wrecked the realm.)

literal: He prized dyed silk's fine quality yet was idle toward jade-carving's lasting blessing.
idiomatic: He prized the good fiber of dyed silk yet was slack toward the lasting blessing of carved jade.

literal: Employ Guan Zhong and rule reached perfection; dote on Duke Huan's favorite and disorder rose.
idiomatic: Use a Guan Zhong and order comes; dote on a Duke Huan's favorite and chaos rises.

literal: (When Zu Xiaozheng held power, court and countryside drew together and government and punishment had their thread.)
idiomatic: (When Zu Xiaozheng held power, court and countryside moved as one and law and policy had a thread to follow.)

literal: Luotuopa and the rest hated Xiaozheng for binding them by law and slandered him until he was removed.
idiomatic: Luotuopa and his circle hated Xiaozheng for binding them with law and slandered him out of office.

literal: Then edicts grew benighted and perverse, down to ruin.
idiomatic: Edicts then grew benighted and perverse, all the way to extinction.

literal: Truly slack and negligent in measuring government; he grieved how swiftly the divine banishment came.
idiomatic: He was slack and negligent in measuring government, and grieved how swiftly heaven's banishment came.

literal: First the rotting fish at Pingyang; next bamboo splitting at Taiyuan.
idiomatic: First the rotting fish at Pingyang, then bamboo splitting at Taiyuan.

literal: A small setback at Jin province and he abandoned the army back to Bing; he would not hold Bing either, fleeing toward Ye.
idiomatic: A small reverse at Jin province and he abandoned the army for Bing; he would not hold Bing either, but fled toward Ye.

literal: Indeed the new and full moons had not altered; then □□□□□□□; when the capital □ rose and fell, he bore thoughts of ancestral tombs submerged.
idiomatic: The moon's phases had barely shifted when [text missing]; when the capital [text missing] rose and fell he nursed the fear that his family's graves had been drowned.

literal: Lost sight of the ruler to judge men; all rushed to roost and pick their tree.
idiomatic: Men forgot the ruler and judged only people; each hurried to roost and choose his tree.

literal: Six horses in turmoil, a thousand officials scattered in flight.
idiomatic: Six horses thrashed in chaos; a thousand officials scattered in the rout.

literal: No winter melon to cure hunger, no autumn fireflies to light the night.
idiomatic: There was no winter melon to ease hunger, no autumn firefly to light the night.

literal: (It was deep winter, hence no such things.)
idiomatic: (It was deep winter, so such things did not exist.)

literal: Vengeance rose within the boat; Hu and Yue were born at the chariot hub.
idiomatic: Enemies rose within the boat; Hu and Yue sprang from the chariot's hub.

literal: Prince Ande's one battle invited the civil and military remnant's blessing.
idiomatic: Prince Ande's single battle drew what blessing civil and military remnants could offer.

literal: Corpses strewn thick as wild grass; blood black-yellow piled into valleys.
idiomatic: Corpses lay thick as wild grass; blood black and yellow heaped into valleys.

literal: (After the Later Sovereign fled, Prince Ande Yan Zong gathered the embers and fought at Bing by night, killing several thousand.
idiomatic: (After the Later Sovereign fled, Prince Ande Yan Zong gathered the embers, fought at Bing by night, and killed several thousand.)

literal: The Zhou ruler wished to withdraw; Qi generals who had surrendered to Zhou told him the truth, so he stayed until dawn and Ande was defeated.)
idiomatic: The Zhou ruler meant to pull back, but Qi generals who had surrendered to Zhou told him the true situation, so he held on until dawn and Ande was defeated.)

literal: Though heaven's mandate could not come twice, still he deemed dying at the temple and weeping the nobler act.
idiomatic: Heaven's mandate might not come twice, yet he still thought it nobler to die at the ancestral temple and weep.

literal: Then he was charged with governing a commandery, holding a key road and asking the ford.
idiomatic: Then they charged him with governing a commandery, holding a key road and asking after the crossing.

literal: (He was made governor of Pingyuan, holding the river ford, as part of the plan to flee to Chen.)
idiomatic: (Zhitui was made governor of Pingyuan, holding the river crossing, as part of the plan to flee to Chen.)

literal: Like calling out to ferry and cross water; countryside guided them to a good neighbor.
idiomatic: It was like shouting for a ferry to cross the waters; the countryside would guide them to a friendly neighbor.

literal: (They agreed that if the battle below Ye did not succeed, he would enter Chen with Zhitui.)
idiomatic: (They agreed that if the fight below Ye failed, the sovereign would enter Chen with Zhitui.)

literal: Not ashamed of lodging with a lord's kindness; willing to be a guest in Decaying Splendour.
idiomatic: He was not ashamed to accept a lord's sheltering kindness and was willing to be a guest in Decaying Splendour.

literal: Suddenly after agreement he repented midway; he disguised estrangement in private while showing kinship in public.
idiomatic: Suddenly, after words were given, he repented halfway; private coldness wore the mask of public warmth.

literal: Trusted flattery's plots from the princess; competed to fall into treacherous ministers' traps.
idiomatic: He trusted the princess's flattery and plots, and all raced to fall into treacherous ministers' snares.

literal: (Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the rest did not wish to go south, and feared that losing the Qi ruler would mean guilt before Zhou, so they estranged Zhitui.
idiomatic: (Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the rest did not wish to flee south and feared that if they lost the Qi ruler Zhou would blame them, so they drove a wedge between sovereign and Zhitui.)

literal: Therefore the Qi ruler left Zhitui to hold Pingyuan city while he demanded boats to cross the Ji toward Qing province.
idiomatic: So the Qi ruler left Zhitui to hold Pingyuan while he demanded boats to cross the Ji toward Qing province.

literal: Anagong asked to garrison Jizhou himself and then reported to the Qi ruler, "No bandits—do not hurry."
idiomatic: Anagong asked to garrison Jizhou himself, then sent word to the Qi ruler: "There are no bandits—do not hurry."

literal: Thus he guided the Zhou army to pursue the Qi ruler and overtake him.)
idiomatic: So he guided the Zhou army in pursuit until they overtook the Qi ruler.)

literal: Once nine domains answered to command; now eight feet are subject to others.
idiomatic: Once the nine domains answered to his command; now even eight feet of body belong to another.

literal: The twenty-eight-year term must run out; the hundred-six count suddenly heaps up.
idiomatic: The twenty-eight-year span had to end; the hundred-six calamity number suddenly piled up.

literal: (Li Muchu of Zhao commandery was skilled in astronomy and calculation; at Qi's founding he calculated that rule would end in twenty-eight years.
idiomatic: (Li Muchu of Zhao commandery was skilled in astronomy and reckoning; at Qi's founding he calculated that the dynasty would end in twenty-eight years.)

literal: When the time came it perished as foretold.)
idiomatic: When the term came it fell exactly as he had said.)

literal: One life, three transformations; he tasted bitterness of tea and pungency of smartweed.
idiomatic: In one life he knew three transformations and tasted tea's bitterness and smartweed's bite.

literal: (At Yangdu he met Hou Jing's killing of Emperor Jianwen and usurpation; at Jiangling he met Emperor Xiaoyuan's ruin; here he became a man of a fallen state for the third time.)
idiomatic: (At Yangdu he lived through Hou Jing's murder of Emperor Jianwen and seizure of the throne; at Jiangling through Emperor Xiaoyuan's destruction; here he was a man of a ruined state for the third time.)

literal: Birds burned the forest and broke pinions; fish lost water and exposed scales.
idiomatic: Birds burned the forest and broke their pinions; fish lost the water and bared their scales.

literal: Alas the universe's vast emptiness; ashamed that nowhere could hold his person.
idiomatic: Alas—the universe's vast emptiness; he was ashamed that nowhere could hold his body.

literal: When one faults oneself in lawsuit, only then does enlightenment break through native truth.
idiomatic: Only when a man accuses himself does the veil lift from inborn truth.

literal: Far rejecting sagehood and abandoning wisdom, vainly locking duty to bind benevolence.
idiomatic: He had rejected the sages from afar and cast wisdom aside, vainly locking duty to chain benevolence.

literal: All the world drowned and he wished to save it; the kingly way was choked and he sought to clear it.
idiomatic: The whole world was drowning and he wished to save it; the kingly way was choked and he sought to open it.

literal: First he carried stone to fill the sea; in the end he shouldered spear to enter Qin.
idiomatic: First he carried stone to fill the sea; in the end he bore a spear toward Qin.

literal: Lost Shouling's old pace; facing the great road he hesitated.
idiomatic: He lost Shouling's old stride and halted on the great road, unable to go forward.

literal: Had he only hid beneath thatch, content as a field hand—
idiomatic: Had he only hidden under thatch and been content as a man behind the plow—

literal: no reading books and learning sword, never rubbing palms to anoint himself, yielding bright pearls to delight in low estate, declining white jade to dwell in poverty—Yao and Shun could not glorify such plainness, Jie and Zhou could not stain such clear dust.
idiomatic: never reading books and learning the sword, never rubbing his palms to grease his way upward, yielding bright pearls to rejoice in low estate, declining white jade to rest in poverty—Yao and Shun could not have glorified such plainness, Jie and Zhou could not have stained such clear dust.

literal: Whence did this extremity come? Whence did this disgrace arise?
idiomatic: Whence came this extremity? Whence this disgrace?

literal: From now on I dare not blame heaven or weep for the unicorn.
idiomatic: From now on I dare not blame heaven or weep for the unicorn.

literal: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder Siyu, the younger Minchu—names that forgot nothing of their roots.
idiomatic: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder Siyu, the younger Minchu—names that would not let them forget where they came from.

literal: Zhitui's collected works survive; Siyu wrote the preface and record himself.
idiomatic: Zhitui's collected works survive; Siyu wrote the preface and catalogue himself.

literal: Yuan Shuang, styled Yuanming, of Chen commandery, was grandson of Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.
idiomatic: Yuan Shuang, styled Yuanming, came from Chen commandery and was grandson of Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.

literal: His father Junfang was Liang attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: His father Junfang had been Liang attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: Shuang, in Xiao Zhuang's time, as attendant-in-ordinary bore tribute missions.
idiomatic: In Xiao Zhuang's time Shuang served as attendant-in-ordinary on missions bearing tribute.

literal: When Zhuang fell he was assigned to Prince of Langye Yan's staff as army counsellor, entered the hall, and was promoted grand palace counsellor.
idiomatic: When Zhuang fell he was attached to Prince of Langye Yan as army counsellor, entered the Forest of Literature Hall, and rose to grand palace counsellor.

literal: Wei Daoxun was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
idiomatic: Wei Daoxun came from Duling in Jingzhao.

literal: His great-grandfather Su followed Liu Yizhen across the river.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Su followed Liu Yizhen when he crossed the Yangtze.

literal: His grandfather Chong, coming from Song into Wei, lived at Luoyang in Henan and rose to governor of Huashan.
idiomatic: His grandfather Chong came from Song into Wei, settled at Luoyang in Henan, and rose to governor of Huashan.

literal: Daoxun with his elder brothers Daomi, Daojian, and Daoru were all early famed for letters.
idiomatic: Daoxun and his elder brothers Daomi, Daojian, and Daoru were all known early for literary talent.

literal: Daomi, in Wei's Yongxi era, was libationer of an opening establishment.
idiomatic: Daomi, in Wei's Yongxi era, was libationer of an opening establishment.

literal: He suffered mental confusion and was confined at home.
idiomatic: He fell into mental confusion and lived out his days confined at home.

literal: Daojian died at the end of Tianbao as vice minister of agriculture.
idiomatic: Daojian died at the end of Tianbao while serving as vice minister of agriculture.

literal: Daoru served through the posts of gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Daoru served as gentleman of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat.

literal: Daoxun, in early Wuping, was left military section chief in the Secretariat, added unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry, entered the hall, and was made unhampered regular attendant.
idiomatic: In early Wuping Daoxun was left military section chief in the Secretariat, then added unhampered attendant of scattered cavalry, entered the hall, and became unhampered regular attendant.

literal: Jiang Gan, styled Ji, was a man of Jiyang.
idiomatic: Jiang Gan, styled Ji, came from Jiyang.

literal: His grandfather Rouzhi was director of the right section under Southern Qi.
idiomatic: His grandfather Rouzhi had been Southern Qi's director of the right section.

literal: His uncle Ge was Liang director of punishments at court.
idiomatic: His uncle Ge had been Liang director of punishments at court.

literal: Gan, at the end of Liang, was gentleman of the Yellow Gate; on a mission to Huainan he was seized by a border general and sent to Ye.
idiomatic: At the end of Liang Gan was gentleman of the Yellow Gate; on a mission to Huainan he was seized by a border general and sent to Ye.

literal: He was gradually promoted to marshal of Zheng province, entered the hall, was made senior aide to the Grand Commandant, and transferred to crown prince household head.
idiomatic: He rose gradually to marshal of Zheng province, entered the hall, became senior aide to the Grand Commandant, and was transferred to crown prince household head.

literal: When Qi fell he fled back to Jianye.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he fled back to Jianye.

literal: He died as director of punishments at court.
idiomatic: He ended his career as director of punishments at court.

literal: Sui Yu, styled Daoxian, was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Sui Yu, styled Daoxian, came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

literal: His father Ji was Liang governor of Beiping.
idiomatic: His father Ji had been Liang governor of Beiping.

literal: Daoxian at cap maturity was nominated eminent scholar by his province.
idiomatic: At cap maturity Daoxian was nominated eminent scholar by his province.

literal: In Tianbao he joined discussion on ritual ordinances and served as Jin province expedition staff clerk, grand judge, and chariot-of-the-court commandant.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he took part in drafting ritual ordinances and served as Jin province expedition staff clerk, grand judge, and chariot-of-the-court commandant.

literal: He entered the hall.
idiomatic: He entered the Forest of Literature Hall.

literal: He was promoted supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and soon also director of the sacrifices department.
idiomatic: He was promoted to supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and soon also director of the sacrifices department.

literal: In Kaihuang of Sui he died as Lu province marshal.
idiomatic: In Sui's Kaihuang era he died while serving as marshal of Lu province.
